dana: Quick flag — onboarding prism-34k-int2hybrid to staging. After running a long "staggered-header-burst" prefill (mix of short headers + multi-paragraph blobs) up to ~31k tokens we consistently see a one-slot KV index shift and downstream token drift compared to fp32. Repro and compact logs below.

 dana: minimal repro (staging):
```
# run harness - small reproducer
python -m tests.kv_long_repro --model prism-34k-int2hybrid --quant int2hybrid --prefill tests/data/staggered_burst.txt --max-tokens 31200 --kv-inspect --kv-dump 12:6 --preserve-order false
```

dana: concise log excerpt:
```
kv_inspect: idx=30998 fp_before=0x5f7bcd fp_after_prefill=0x5f7bce (bump)
gen: mismatch pos=30999 expected="ed" got="e"
```

pierre: only on int2hybrid? any float32 runs?
dana: float32 matches baseline. int2hybrid shows bump. model cfg snippet: `rotary_base: 10000.0, pos_scale: 1.012, rotary_interp: linear, rotary_clip: 1e-6`

alex: what are tile/stride args?
dana: default tiled mapping: `--kv-tile 128 --kv-stride 16`. No preserve-order. Also using prefetcher v3 async merge.

lee: three quick experiments to isolate: 1) `--preserve-order true` (rule out merge race), 2) dense mapping `--kv-stride 1 --kv-tile 65536`, 3) switch interp `rotary_interp: nearest` and try `pos_scale: 1.0`. If dense fixes it, it's mapping arithmetic; if preserve-order fixes it, prefetch race likely; if nearest helps, interpolation amplification of quant noise.

pierre: also try running with `--kv-slot-sanity-check` (short-lived assert mode) to catch slot collisions at insertion time. If collision occurs, we should log `slot,claimed_by,existing_key` and fail-fast.

dana: running preserve-order + dense-index + nearest-interp now. Adding a tiny dump helper to print `idx,slot,key_hash,fp_before,fp_after,ctx_snippet` so diffs are compact. ETA ~25m.

ci-bot: Canary deploy prism-34k-int2hybrid -> staging started (canary-id: cb-20260711-13). Tests queued: kv_long_repro x3. Logs at /var/log/onboard/prism/cb-13.log

alex: FYI: if we see consistent +1 bump, check prefetcher v3's header trimming logic; I remember a subtle off-by-one when streaming headers with mixed length. Also double-check int2hybrid packing alignment: misaligned copy could shift subsequent keys by one slot.

pierre: good call. If dense mapping still bumps, attempt a short repeat-only prefill to reach the same absolute idx (to separate absolute position vs content pattern). If repeat-only doesn't reproduce, it's likely interleaving ordering.

dana: will attach trimmed CSV diff (`idx,slot,key_hash,fp_before,fp_after,token_window`) when runs complete. Thanks all. :coffee:
